children: A few consumer staples favorites outperformed on Thursday in early action as the broad market retreated again. Kroger
showed an early gain of 2.8%, and Dollar General

rose 2.5%. In the background, Treasury yields continued to rise on the expectation of more Federal Reserve rate hikes, and oil prices broke higher once again. The combination has investors turning more defensive into names that typically weather turbulent markets.
is still down 5.2% on a year-to-date basis, and Dollar General
is off 7.2%. However, both consumer staples stocks have a consensus Buy rating across both Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha analysts. Seeking Alpha analyst
maintained his Buy rating on Kroger
after its earnings report, citing a wide margin of safety at 10.9X forward earnings and superior shareholder yield versus industry peers. Meanwhile, Seeking Alpha analyst
continues to capitalize on value-oriented consumers amid a challenging macroeconomic environment.

title: Investors turn defensive, bidding up Kroger and Dollar General
